allocation_impact: A thin caller-owned bounded ingress adapter uses checked cumulative accounting across all inbound handshake reads and rejects an increment that would overflow or raise the total above 65,536 bytes before supplying any bytes from that increment to stock rustls. Native rustls per-message and backing limits separately protect library-owned memory.
boundary_tests: 65,536 cumulative inbound handshake bytes accepted where semantically valid and every coupled limit passes, including across multiple read segmentations
65,537 cumulative inbound handshake bytes rejected as UNAVAILABLE before any bytes from the over-limit increment are supplied to rustls
Checked-add overflow rejected before supplying the increment to rustls; native per-message/backing limits remain a separate library-owned-memory bound
notes: Fixed configured cap, not required actual occupancy/size. Internal boundary adds no wire enum. Written boundary tests are future implementation obligations, not executed proof. Fixed profile per #342 addendum; meaningful smaller profiles unsupported. Source-age/authentication constraints remain independent. The caller-owned adapter enforces this cumulative bound before bytes enter stock rustls; proof of a native aggregate 65,536-byte rustls bound is not required. Native rustls per-message and backing limits remain separate. Exceeding the transport/PKI envelope makes the source unavailable. Persistent floors/denials/receipts are never evicted to meet resident limits; no automatic retry, background refresh or coalesced waiter fanout.
